text_blocks.snippet: To get UK residency (Indefinite Leave to Remain - ILR), you typically need to have lived in the UK for a continuous period on an eligible visa, usually 5 years. Some routes, like the UK Ancestry visa, may allow for settlement after 5 years, while others, like long residence (10 years), may have different requirements. You also need to meet other requirements, including English language proficiency and passing the Life in the UK test.
snippet_highlighted_words: you typically need to have lived in the UK for a continuous period on an eligible visa, usually 5 years

text_blocks.snippet: Types of UK Residency Visas and Eligibility:

list.snippet: Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR): This grants you the right to live in the UK without immigration restrictions.
Long Residence: You can apply for ILR after 10 years of continuous legal residence in the UK.
Family Visa: If you are a spouse or partner of a British citizen or someone settled in the UK, you may be eligible for ILR after 5 years.
UK Ancestry Visa: If you have a grandparent born in the UK, you can apply for this visa and potentially qualify for ILR after 5 years.
Skilled Worker visa: A route for skilled workers sponsored by a UK employer, potentially leading to ILR after 5 years of continuous employment.
Innovator Founder visa/Global Talent visa: May allow for settlement after 3 years.
High Potential Individual (HPI) visa: Requires a qualification awarded within the last 5 years.
Tier 1 Investor visa: Requires a substantial investment in the UK.
Continuous Residence: You must have lived in the UK for a continuous period on an eligible visa.
Absence Limit: Generally, you cannot have been absent from the UK for more than 180 days in any 12-month period.
Financial Requirements: You must demonstrate the ability to support yourself and any dependents financially without relying on public funds.
English Language Proficiency: You must meet the required English language level.
Life in the UK Test: You must pass the Life in the UK test, which assesses your knowledge of British life and culture.

list.title: Qualifying Period:
list.snippet: The standard qualifying period for ILR is generally 5 years, but this can vary depending on the visa route.

list.title: Continuous Residence:
list.snippet: Gaps in your residence can affect your eligibility for ILR.

list.title: Specific Visa Requirements:
list.snippet: Each visa route has its own specific requirements, so it's crucial to understand the rules for your particular visa.

list.title: Consult an Immigration Advisor:
list.snippet: Due to the complexity of UK immigration rules, it's recommended to seek professional advice from an immigration advisor, especially for complex cases.

text_blocks.snippet: There have been proposals to increase the standard qualifying period for ILR to 10 years, with some exceptions.
